Board discussion document, January 2027
Parcelbird
Board (two founders, two investors)
Synthetic benchmark data from the briefing pack; all figures fictional

slides.title: Executive summary

paragraphs.text: Executive summary
Do not launch Parcelbird Now in 2027: grow the software business, and reopen the question on four conditions
Quick commerce is growing fast, but neither incumbent makes money on an order
–	Zipcart loses $1.90 and QuickBasket $3.40 on each order
At our customer sites' median, each order loses $6.17 after site costs
–	On order value alone, it would need a $63 basket to break even
Customers try the service, but few stay long enough to repay their acquisition cost
–	Only 22% of pop-up customers were still ordering in month three
–	A retained customer repays its $38 cost only after about 15 months
The plan breaches the 12-month runway floor even if everything goes right
–	The plan needs 1.3 times the cash we can spend above the floor
–	At median economics, nine stores would lose about $18M a year
Scaling the software instead costs $0.8M a year and keeps grocers as customers
–	Late-stage grocers alone hold contracts worth 21% of today's ARR
–	A one-store pilot would spend $2.6M re-testing what we already know

CASE  Zipcart, the national leader, in its densest city, Q4 2025
Losing money nationally, even at scale
Charged customers more and cut discounts
Impact
▪	Largest US operator, with $1,200M of revenue in 2025
▪	Lost $1.90 on the average order across its network
▪	Its densest city was the best place to try to turn a profit
▪	Added a new $3.99 service fee on every order
▪	Cut promotions to 1% of order value
▪	Did not rely on running stores more efficiently
